title: The hour everyone marks
hookLine: vespers, maghrib prayer, sandhya, Shabbat candles: many traditions mark dusk, each for its own reasons

lines: BELLS, A CALL, A LAMP, CANDLES.
cards: Every evening, a line moves around the planet: day on one side, night on the other. As it sweeps over each town, something happens in a lot of places at once. In a monastery, bells ring for evening prayer.
In a mosque, the call to the sunset prayer goes out. In a Hindu home, someone lights a lamp and sits for the evening rite. On Friday, in Jewish homes, candles are lit just before the sun goes down.
Nobody planned this together. Each has its own history and its own reasons. This new week is all about sunset, starting with the hour everyone marks.

teach.b: Take them one at a time. Vespers is the Christian evening prayer, from the Latin word for evening.
A Psalm long sung at this hour asks: "let my prayer be set forth before thee as incense; and the lifting up of my hands as the evening sacrifice."

Maghrib is the sunset prayer in Islam, prayed just after the sun has set. The same Arabic word can also mean the west, where the sun goes down. And during Ramadan, sunset is the moment the day's fast is broken.
Sandhya is Sanskrit for a joining, the seam where one part of the day meets the next. Prayers called sandhya vandana are traditionally performed at these seams: dawn, noon and dusk.
And Shabbat, as last week showed, begins at sunset on Friday, which is why the candles are lit before the sun goes down.
In the Jewish calendar, every day begins at evening, following Genesis: there was evening, and there was morning. Four traditions, four different understandings of what the hour is for.
What they share is a noticing: the moment day turns into night deserves to be marked, not scrolled through. The light changes. The birds get loud, then quiet.
Something ends. This week borrows only that noticing. It asks for nothing more than your eyes, for the few minutes it takes the sun to go.

how: Vespers or evening prayer is prayed in many churches and monasteries, Muslims pray maghrib just after sunset, sandhya vandana is traditionally performed at dawn, noon and dusk, and Jews light Shabbat candles before sunset on Friday, each for its own reasons.

games.q: it's Ramadan, and the sun has just set. what happens for many Muslims now?
o: the fast is broken, and maghrib is prayed.
games.why: sunset breaks the day's fast, and maghrib, the sunset prayer, is prayed just after the sun goes down.

practice: Look up when sunset is where you live today, and picture where you could see the western sky: a window, a doorstep, a street corner, a park. Picture the phone put away, in a pocket or back inside.
Then picture the light going gold, then orange, then gray, while you just watch.
